fields.title: Stop worktree land silently committing endless's own files and advising a destructive rebase fix
fields.description: At land time, `endless worktree land` quietly commits any of endless's own files (ledger, verbs.jsonl, snapshots, config.json) that it finds uncommitted in the main checkout, and -- when the rebase conflicts -- it used to tell the user to run a `git checkout` that throws the branch's version of those files away unexamined. This task drops the silent commit, so that a writer bug leaving those files uncommitted gets surfaced instead of buried, and replaces the conflict advice with a message that names what conflicted and how to inspect it.
fields.analysis:
## What the two parts mean, in plain terms

**1. Land silently commits endless's own files.** Before rebasing, land looks at whatever is uncommitted in the main checkout. Anything it recognizes as a file endless itself writes -- the ledger, `verbs.jsonl`, snapshots, `config.json` -- it stages and commits as "Endless: auto-record session activity" without telling anyone. The argument for removing this: those files are supposed to be committed the moment they are written, so land should never find them uncommitted. When it does, that is a bug being papered over. Land should stop and name the files instead of sweeping them up.

**2. Its advice after a failed rebase could destroy work.** When the rebase conflicted, the error message told the user to run `git checkout main -- <endless's file patterns>`, which discards the branch's version of those files without anyone looking at them. If the conflict was real, that silently loses work. The message should name what conflicted and show how to inspect it.

## Where this stands (verified 2026-08-25)

- **Part 2 is done**, shipped separately under E-1417 (commit b1efcc2). `_rebase_conflict_message()` names the commit that failed to replay and the conflicting files, and offers the `git checkout` recovery only when *every* conflicting path is an endless-managed file; otherwise it presents recoveries as candidates to judge between, flagged as possibly wrong.
- **Part 1's premise does not hold.** The auto-commit step still fires: 53 "Endless: auto-record session activity" commits on main, four of them on 2026-08-24. Endless-managed files still arrive at land uncommitted despite E-1206 and E-1208 committing at write time, so removing the step today would turn routine lands into refusals. Why they still arrive dirty is the open question underneath part 1.

fields.text:
# Plan

Three landable increments. Each leaves the tree green and shippable; do not
start the next until the previous has landed.

## Increment 1 — the tables, written but not yet authoritative

New schema change file `internal/schema/changes/e-2063-session-instances.sql`,
mirrored into `internal/schema/schema.sql`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS session_instances (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    session_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    harness       TEXT    NOT NULL,
    first_seen_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now')),
    last_event_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now')),
    ended_at      TEXT,
    recap         TEXT,
    recap_through TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id, harness)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claude_cli_sessions (
    instance_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    harness     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (harness = 'claude_cli'),
    uuid        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    FOREIGN KEY (instance_id, harness)
        REFERENCES session_instances (id, harness)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS session_instances_by_session
    ON session_instances (session_id, first_seen_at);
```

NO `UNIQUE (session_id) WHERE ended_at IS NULL`. `ended_at` is display-only —
see the analysis; adding that index re-opens a settled decision.

Backfill in the same change file: one instance per existing `sessions` row,
`first_seen_at` from `sessions.started_at`, `last_event_at` from
`sessions.last_activity`, `harness` from `sessions.platform`, `ended_at` set
when `state='ended'`, and a `claude_cli_sessions` row carrying
`sessions.session_id` where that is non-empty and `platform='claude'`.

Nothing reads the new tables yet. Land here.

## Increment 2 — resolution moves to the instance

`sessions.session_id` stays in place and keeps being written, so this increment
is reversible; it stops being the resolution key, not the stored value.

- `monitor.GetActiveSession(uuid)` resolves uuid -> `claude_cli_sessions` ->
  `session_instances` -> `sessions`, returning the Endless session.
- `monitor.TouchSession` upserts the INSTANCE (bumping `last_event_at`, clearing
  a stale `ended_at`), and upserts the `sessions` row only when no instance
  matches the uuid.
- SessionStart: when the window/task already has a session and the uuid is new,
  append an instance rather than inserting a `sessions` row. `payload.Source`
  (`startup`/`resume`/`clear`/`compact`) is currently read nowhere; read it here
  and treat anything other than `startup` as continuation.
- Close the prior instance (`ended_at`) when a clear appends a new one.
- `session_messages.session_id` FKs `sessions(session_id)` — the uuid, not the
  id. Re-point it at `session_instances.id` so a clear gives later transcript
  rows a new parent and no prior row is rewritten.
- Move `platform` off `sessions`; `session_instances.harness` is the single
  discriminator.

Re-parenting rule for everything that references `sessions.id`, applied in
increment 3 but decided here. Split by whether the row describes a CONVERSATION
or the WORK:

- **Per-conversation -> `session_instances.id`**: `session_messages`
  (transcripts), `session_gates` (relay checkpoints and the minimizer corpus
  triples — both are per-turn), `report_labels`, `session_navigations`
  (from/to are acts of navigating, which happen inside one conversation).
- **Per-session -> unchanged, still `sessions.id`**: `session_tasks`,
  `decisions.origin_session_id`, `task_landings`, `project_next_events`. These
  describe the work, not the conversation that produced it, and a task's
  relation to its session must survive a clear.

Getting this split wrong in the per-conversation direction is the failure that
matters: re-pointing those rows at the surviving session would flatten every
prior conversation into one and destroy exactly the history this redesign
exists to preserve.

## Increment 3 — the collapse, and the CLI

- Re-parent the multiple `sessions` rows per task that exist today (E-1307 has
  7; 1362 and 1322 have 6). NOTHING IS DISCARDED: the earliest row by
  `started_at` remains the session, and every other row BECOMES AN INSTANCE of
  it, carrying its own uuid, timestamps and `ended_at`. Seven conversations stay
  seven conversations; they stop being seven sessions. Re-point the referencing
  tables per the split above — per-conversation rows follow their conversation
  to its instance, per-session rows follow the survivor.
- `resume` refuses when a session has 2+ instances with `ended_at IS NULL`:
  print them ordered by `first_seen_at` ASC with ordinal, `first_seen_at`,
  `last_event_at`, message count and recap, and exit non-zero. Never close one
  automatically. `--instance <ordinal|uuid>` selects.
- `resume` and `goto --resume` share ONE resolver.
- Delete `spawn --new-session`. Replace with `--fresh-context` if the
  "do not inherit prior context into the handoff" behaviour is still wanted.
- Split `spawn --reopen` into `reopen` (task-status verb) and `resume` (session
  verb; restores the worktree, navigates when a live owner exists).

# Verification

`tests/tasks/e-2063-verify.sh`, fail-fast on units then end-to-end through the
real hook against the sandbox DB (drive it with an explicit `--config-dir`, per
`tests/tasks/e-1953-verify.sh` — without that flag the hook's PinMainDB sends
writes to the REAL ledger).

1. A clear appends: feed SessionStart with a NEW uuid and `source=clear` for a
   window whose session exists; assert exactly one `sessions` row for the task
   before and after, and one more `session_instances` row after.
2. Resume does not append: same, `source=resume` with the existing uuid; assert
   the instance count is unchanged.
3. The prior instance is closed on a clear; the surviving one has
   `ended_at IS NULL`.
4. A stale `ended_at` blocks nothing: leave two instances open, insert a third,
   assert it succeeds. This is the regression guard on the rejected index.
5. `resume` with 2+ open instances exits non-zero, lists them ordered by
   `first_seen_at` ASC, and closes nothing — assert `ended_at` values are
   identical before and after.
6. `--instance` selects by both ordinal and uuid.
7. A `claude_cli_sessions` row cannot attach to a non-`claude_cli` instance —
   assert the composite FK rejects it.
8. Migration preserves history, asserted as a conservation law rather than a
   row count: for each task, `COUNT(session_instances)` after == `COUNT(sessions)`
   before, and every pre-migration uuid is still reachable. Then per-conversation
   rows: no `session_gates` / `session_messages` / `report_labels` row may end up
   parented to an instance whose uuid differs from the session uuid it had
   before. That is the assertion that catches a flattening migration; a bare
   pre/post row count would not.
9. `sessions.platform` is gone and nothing references it.

Not verifiable by test: whether one open instance per session is actually
maintained in the field. Nothing enforces it at the storage layer by design —
that is E-1983's invariant gate plus write-once `task_id`.

fields.outcome: Obsolete: conflicts with the one-worktree-per-task invariant. This task would add 'endless worktree add --purpose verify' to create a SIBLING 'e-NNN-verify' worktree, and says so explicitly — it exists to work around the 'no create verb' lock. E-1643 (completed) settled the opposite: REMOVE the named-alternate worktree capability, collapse to one canonical worktree plus sandbox per task, and model multi-checkout needs (A-B, run-while-edit, bisect, ad-hoc testing) as CHILD TASKS. Mike confirmed there that the named alternate is a capability he has never used and is willing to drop. The verify-isolation need it was filed for was met differently: the Tier-0 runner (E-1603) isolates per run with its own temp HOME and XDG, not a second checkout. The 'endless worktree' group remains read-only by design; creation stays with 'task claim'.

Obsolete: the namespace it protects does not exist. This task would pick a collision strategy for branch names derived from a short-id prefix of a session UUID, for 'session-flavor' worktrees under E-971 Layer F. Worktrees are named 'e-NNN' from the task id, one per task, per E-1643's collapse — there is no session-flavored worktree and no short-id prefix to collide in. It was filed as a 'maybe so it is not forgotten'; the design it hedged against was not taken.

Obsolete: the fix it proposes was decided against. This task would have Python's complete_item null sessions.active_task_id for any session pointing at a just-confirmed task, so a confirm typed outside the hook path could not leave a stale binding. The gap is real — complete_item still never touches active_task_id — but auto-clearing is the behaviour Endless deliberately does not want: E-1303 states 'do NOT auto-clear (the user may want to keep the binding for follow-up work)', and the explicit verb shipped instead as 'endless task release', which drops a session's claim on demand. Releasing on confirm would take that choice away. If the stale binding needs more than a manual release, that belongs to E-1303's prompt-and-flags design, not here.

Obsolete: it would support the path the invariant now forbids. This task would have 'endless task start' auto-create a .endless.worktree.json companion when cwd is a worktree that lacks one — filed because a hand-made 'git worktree add' produces a worktree Endless refuses to adopt. That refusal is now the intended behaviour: CLAUDE.md states never create a worktree by hand, 'task claim' creates and wires yours, and E-1643 collapsed to one canonical worktree per task. 'task start' itself is hidden, superseded by 'task claim', which writes the companion as part of creation. Teaching Endless to adopt hand-made worktrees would re-open the proliferation E-1643 closed. The companion file itself is unchanged and still written; only this adoption path is dropped.

Obsolete per ED-1550: task management is not work that needs a task. This asked to split E-968 into sub-epics and reparent its 53 children, with sign-off before any move. That is a session's ad-hoc housekeeping, and holding it as a backlog item for three months is exactly the filing reflex ED-1550 names — the default response to a finding is to tell the user, not to file. The work was done directly in session ES-1142 (2026-08-25): the drifted children were triaged, the dead ones closed with recorded outcomes, and the reparenting decided in conversation rather than through a task. The mechanism it wished for now exists anyway (epic type with auto-derived status, E-1537), and the proven pattern is converting a workstream to an epic in place — as E-971 was — rather than inventing new sub-epics.

# Plan

Three landable increments. Each leaves the tree green and shippable; do not
start the next until the previous has landed.

## Increment 1 — the tables, written but not yet authoritative

New schema change file `internal/schema/changes/e-2063-session-instances.sql`,
mirrored into `internal/schema/schema.sql`.

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS session_instances (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    session_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    harness       TEXT    NOT NULL,
    first_seen_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now')),
    last_event_at TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S','now')),
    ended_at      TEXT,
    recap         TEXT,
    recap_through TEXT,
    UNIQUE (id, harness)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claude_cli_sessions (
    instance_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    harness     TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (harness = 'claude_cli'),
    uuid        TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    FOREIGN KEY (instance_id, harness)
        REFERENCES session_instances (id, harness)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS session_instances_by_session
    ON session_instances (session_id, first_seen_at);
```

NO `UNIQUE (session_id) WHERE ended_at IS NULL`. `ended_at` is display-only —
see the analysis; adding that index re-opens a settled decision.

Backfill in the same change file: one instance per existing `sessions` row,
`first_seen_at` from `sessions.started_at`, `last_event_at` from
`sessions.last_activity`, `harness` from `sessions.platform`, `ended_at` set
when `state='ended'`, and a `claude_cli_sessions` row carrying
`sessions.session_id` where that is non-empty and `platform='claude'`.

Nothing reads the new tables yet. Land here.

## Increment 2 — resolution moves to the instance

`sessions.session_id` stays in place and keeps being written, so this increment
is reversible; it stops being the resolution key, not the stored value.

- `monitor.GetActiveSession(uuid)` resolves uuid -> `claude_cli_sessions` ->
  `session_instances` -> `sessions`, returning the Endless session.
- `monitor.TouchSession` upserts the INSTANCE (bumping `last_event_at`, clearing
  a stale `ended_at`), and upserts the `sessions` row only when no instance
  matches the uuid.
- SessionStart: when the window/task already has a session and the uuid is new,
  append an instance rather than inserting a `sessions` row. `payload.Source`
  (`startup`/`resume`/`clear`/`compact`) is currently read nowhere; read it here
  and treat anything other than `startup` as continuation.
- Close the prior instance (`ended_at`) when a clear appends a new one.
- `session_messages.session_id` FKs `sessions(session_id)` — the uuid, not the
  id. Re-point it at `session_instances.id` so a clear gives later transcript
  rows a new parent and no prior row is rewritten.
- Move `platform` off `sessions`; `session_instances.harness` is the single
  discriminator.

## The governing rule

**Any field that is a fact about the unique harness conversation moves to
`session_instances`. Anything that is a fact about the WORK stays on
`sessions`.** Applied to rows as well as columns, that is the whole migration —
and it is why keeping the FIRST `sessions.id` of a set loses nothing: once the
conversation-specific columns have moved, the surviving row holds only facts
that were never conversation-specific to begin with.

Columns that MOVE to the instance:

| column              | becomes                              |
|---------------------|--------------------------------------|
| `session_id` (uuid) | `claude_cli_sessions.uuid`           |
| `platform`          | `session_instances.harness`          |
| `started_at`        | `session_instances.first_seen_at`    |
| `last_activity`     | `session_instances.last_event_at`    |
| `state`             | per-conversation                     |
| `process_id`        | the process running THIS conversation|
| `transcript_offset` | how far THIS transcript is parsed    |
| `summary`           | per-conversation                     |
| `last_user_prompt`  | per-turn, so per-conversation        |
| `report_bounces`    | per-turn                             |
| `report_exempt`     | per-turn                             |
| `report_runs`       | per-turn                             |

Columns that STAY on `sessions`: `id`, `project_id`, `task_id`, `epic_id`,
`kind_id`, `plan_file_path`, `hidden`, `short_id`. These describe the work and
its durable identity, and must survive a clear.

`summary` moving to the instance collides with the proposed `recap` /
`recap_through`. They are the same idea; pick one name before writing the table
rather than shipping both.

The same rule decides the referencing tables. Per-conversation rows follow their
conversation to its instance: `session_messages` (transcripts), `session_gates`
(relay checkpoints and the minimizer corpus triples — both per-turn),
`report_labels`, `session_navigations`. Per-session rows stay pointed at the
surviving `sessions.id`: `session_tasks`, `decisions.origin_session_id`,
`task_landings`, `project_next_events`.

Getting the per-conversation direction wrong is the failure that matters:
re-pointing those rows at the surviving session would flatten every prior
conversation into one and destroy exactly the history this redesign exists to
preserve.

## Increment 3 — the collapse, and the CLI

- Re-parent the multiple `sessions` rows per task that exist today (E-1307 has
  7; 1362 and 1322 have 6). NOTHING IS DISCARDED: the earliest row by
  `started_at` remains the session, and every other row BECOMES AN INSTANCE of
  it, carrying its own uuid, timestamps and `ended_at`. Seven conversations stay
  seven conversations; they stop being seven sessions. Re-point the referencing
  tables per the split above — per-conversation rows follow their conversation
  to its instance, per-session rows follow the survivor.
- `resume` refuses when a session has 2+ instances with `ended_at IS NULL`:
  print them ordered by `first_seen_at` ASC with ordinal, `first_seen_at`,
  `last_event_at`, message count and recap, and exit non-zero. Never close one
  automatically. `--instance <ordinal|uuid>` selects.
- `resume` and `goto --resume` share ONE resolver.
- Delete `spawn --new-session`; under one-session-per-task it cannot mean what
  it says. OPEN, and NOT yet decided by the requester: whether its one
  legitimate residue — "do not inject the prior conversation's context into the
  handoff" — is still wanted at all, and if so under what name. Do not invent a
  flag for it without asking.
- Split `spawn --reopen` into `reopen` (task-status verb) and `resume` (session
  verb; restores the worktree, navigates when a live owner exists).

# Verification

`tests/tasks/e-2063-verify.sh`, fail-fast on units then end-to-end through the
real hook against the sandbox DB (drive it with an explicit `--config-dir`, per
`tests/tasks/e-1953-verify.sh` — without that flag the hook's PinMainDB sends
writes to the REAL ledger).

1. A clear appends: feed SessionStart with a NEW uuid and `source=clear` for a
   window whose session exists; assert exactly one `sessions` row for the task
   before and after, and one more `session_instances` row after.
2. Resume does not append: same, `source=resume` with the existing uuid; assert
   the instance count is unchanged.
3. The prior instance is closed on a clear; the surviving one has
   `ended_at IS NULL`.
4. A stale `ended_at` blocks nothing: leave two instances open, insert a third,
   assert it succeeds. This is the regression guard on the rejected index.
5. `resume` with 2+ open instances exits non-zero, lists them ordered by
   `first_seen_at` ASC, and closes nothing — assert `ended_at` values are
   identical before and after.
6. `--instance` selects by both ordinal and uuid.
7. A `claude_cli_sessions` row cannot attach to a non-`claude_cli` instance —
   assert the composite FK rejects it.
8. Migration preserves history, asserted as a conservation law rather than a
   row count: for each task, `COUNT(session_instances)` after == `COUNT(sessions)`
   before, and every pre-migration uuid is still reachable. Then per-conversation
   rows: no `session_gates` / `session_messages` / `report_labels` row may end up
   parented to an instance whose uuid differs from the session uuid it had
   before. That is the assertion that catches a flattening migration; a bare
   pre/post row count would not.
9. `sessions.platform` is gone and nothing references it.

Not verifiable by test: whether one open instance per session is actually
maintained in the field. Nothing enforces it at the storage layer by design —
that is E-1983's invariant gate plus write-once `task_id`.

fields.analysis:
# Measured state of `rebuild-db --confirm`, 2026-08-25 (from E-1967, E-2062)

Recorded here so the epic carries the evidence and its children do not have to
re-derive it. Measured against a fresh schema.sql; the abort was reproduced end
to end with the real binary on the modernc driver.

## The command cannot run, and that is currently load-bearing

`DELETE FROM tasks` tries to null `sessions.task_id`; ED-1560's write-once
trigger aborts that; the abort fails the statement and rolls back the whole
transaction. So the command refuses on any project with a bound session.

That refusal is the only thing preventing the rest. Full transitive FK closure
of the same DELETE, second hop included:

    task_landings          CASCADE   destroyed, never restored
    session_gates          CASCADE   destroyed, never restored (via epic_id)
      report_judgments     CASCADE   destroyed  (SECOND HOP)
      report_labels        CASCADE   destroyed  (SECOND HOP)
    sessions.task_id       SET NULL  violates ED-1560
    sessions.epic_id       SET NULL
    session_statuses       SET NULL  (dead feature, removed separately)
    decisions.origin_task_id, tasks.parent_id   SET NULL, both restored

## Four gaps, not one

1. Copy-back covers only tasks, decisions, decision_relations.
2. task_landings IS built by the projector, never copied back, and is destroyed
   by the cascade above.
3. task_deps IS built by the projector, never copied back, and no FK reaches it
   so a rebuild silently leaves every blocking relation stale.
4. The INPUT is polluted. See E-1041, now a child of this epic.

## Traps for the repair

- `tasks_notify_sessions` is AFTER UPDATE ON tasks. Delete-then-insert never
  fires it; an upsert copy-back WOULD, notifying every live session about every
  task whose projected value differs. Suppress the notice triggers around any
  copy-back; e-1969's change file shows the drop-then-recreate shape.
- `task_landings_notify_sessions` is AFTER INSERT, so copying landings back
  announces every historical landing to every live session. The E-2005 schema
  comment calls that replay "harmless" ON THE GROUNDS that rebuild copies back
  only three tables. True today, false the moment the repair lands. Correct it
  in the same commit.
- A projected task_landings.session_id may name a session this machine never
  had; the ledger is shareable, sessions are machine-local. NULL it on copy.
- `PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF` is not the escape. SQLite ignores it inside a
  transaction, so it would fence the whole replacement and leave dangling rows
  on a genuinely-lost id. MaxOpenConns is 1, so the usual pooled-connection
  objection does not apply; the reason is correctness.

## Ordering constraint

Removing `sessions.task_id`'s ON DELETE SET NULL is correct on its own terms: it
contradicts ED-1560, and session_tasks already documents the right shape (no FK
at all, so rows outlive their task). But it also removes the tripwire, turning a
loud refusal into silent loss of the four CASCADE tables. It must land AFTER
this epic makes the rebuild whole, never before. E-2062 guards the interval.

fields.outcome: Obsoleted 2026-08-25 under the backlog-reduction policy: not an immediate pain point, refile if it ever becomes one. Part 2 (non-destructive rebase-conflict message) already shipped separately under E-1417, commit b1efcc2 — _rebase_conflict_message() names the commit that failed to replay and the conflicting files, and offers the 'git checkout <base> -- <globs>' recovery only when every conflicting path is an endless-managed auto-file. Part 1 (drop land's batch auto-commit step) rejected on evidence: the step is original designed behavior from E-971 (2026-05-01), not dead code, and still fires — 53 'Endless: auto-record session activity' commits on main, four of them on 2026-08-24. Its premise, that write-time commits under E-1206/E-1208/E-1275 left nothing for land to auto-commit, is false; removing it would turn routine lands into refusals. No defect was diagnosed and nothing was filed. The abandoned implementation lives only as uncommitted edits in worktree e-1272.

Obsoleted 2026-08-25. E-1366 existed only to pick between reopening E-1272 with narrowed scope or closing it and refiling. That decision is made: E-1272 is obsolete as of 2026-08-25, its recovery-hint half having already shipped under E-1417. E-1366's own premise is also dead — it rested on E-1361's redesign moving verbs.json and snapshots into .git/info/endless/, but E-1361 no longer exists and that directory was never created.

fields.title: Emit events for the mutations the projection needs to rebuild
fields.description: Mutations outside the task and decision domains never reach the ledger, so the projection cannot rebuild the tables that hold them and `rebuild-db` restores only tasks, decisions and decision_relations. Wire the remaining mutations through endless-event. Consolidates E-911 and E-912; the implementor determines which entities still apply and gets user approval on that scope before building.
fields.analysis:
Consolidated 2026-08-25 from three tasks that carried the same sentence — 'Required before projection can rebuild <table>'.

E-910 (sessions): work_started, chat_started, idled, ended, task_completed,
recapped, hidden.
E-911 (projects): registered, updated, renamed, unregistered, purged.
E-912 (notes, conversations, messages): the remaining entity mutations.

Evidence for the scope call, NOT a scope decision — settle it against the tree
at pickup, because this list is a snapshot and the ground moves:

- E-2029 dropped the channel tables, and E-1489 and E-1491 ('Port channel DB
  access', 'Port suggestions DB access') are both obsolete for the same reason.
  So E-912's conversation and message half may have no subject left. Check.
- Sessions are deliberately machine-local runtime state today, and several
  schema comments say so ('session_tasks is live-only session state and is not
  rebuilt from the ledger'). Emitting session events changes that premise, so
  E-910's half is a design question, not just wiring. See E-799's analysis.
- E-1035 (focus events failing the session_id FK on replay) is downstream of
  the same gap and has been folded into E-1041.

Folded in E-1035 (2026-08-25): 'rebuild-db projects task events into a temp DB but skips session events, so focus events fail the session_id FK constraint when replayed. Add ensureSession() to projector.go (mirroring ensureProject) that creates a stub session row when a focus event references one not yet present. Surfaced during E-1030 verification.'

Same class as this task's (a) — the projector meets a reference the projection
does not contain — and the same fix shape as the existing ensureProject. Kept
here rather than as a sibling so the missing-reference problem has one owner.

Note the interaction with E-910: if session mutations ever reach the ledger, the
stub-session workaround stops being needed for focus events specifically. It is
still needed for the pre-E-808 backfill gap, which no future emission fixes.

fields.title: Handle multi-agent write conflicts: detect, park, surface, resolve
fields.description: Concurrent agents can write conflicting state. Resolve conflicting events deterministically at projection time, park invariant violations as conflict records rather than dropping them, and surface those records for a human or agent to resolve with a new event. Consolidates E-815.
fields.analysis:
Consolidated 2026-08-25 from two halves of one mechanism.

E-814 (atomic claim primitive): 'Atomic claim sets assignee + transitions to
in_progress in one event. Conflicts resolved by HLC order at projection time.'
E-815 (conflict surfacing): 'Park invariant violations as conflict records.
Surface in dashboard. Expose via CLI + MCP. AI proposes resolution or escalates.
Resolution is a new event.'

Evidence at consolidation time, NOT a scope decision — re-check at pickup:

- The CLAIM half of E-814 looks largely shipped by unrelated work: task.claimed
  is a live event, ED-1560 makes sessions.task_id write-once with a trigger, and
  E-1967 refuses a spawn onto a task any session ever claimed. What is NOT
  shipped is deterministic conflict RESOLUTION — kairos timestamps exist and
  sort causally, but nothing resolves two conflicting writes by them.
- No conflicts table exists in schema.sql. E-815 is unstarted.

fields.outcome: E-922 raised MaxEventLineBytes from 4KB to 1MB, which is what this task existed to make reachable. The trigger was a 17KB plan file; 1MB is ~60x that and nothing has approached it since. Configurability here would be a knob with no demonstrated turn. Re-file if a real project hits the ceiling.

Shipped by other work. The catch-all text column was split long ago: tasks now carries description, text, analysis, outcome and notes as distinct fields, each with its own update path (E-999 placed analysis before text; E-1601 gave large fields their own placeholder rendering). The 'migration: existing text -> plan field' this task planned already happened piecemeal.

payload.title: Confine the replaced-by annotation to task detail, not tabular listings
payload.description: `task show`'s Status: line gained an inline ` (replaced by E-NNN)` annotation in E-1956. That was intended for the detail view, but the same rendering reaches tabular listings, where it widens the Status column to fit its longest value: 'obsolete (replaced by E-1367)' is roughly three times the width of a bare status. Every row pays that width so that a handful can carry an annotation already discoverable by opening the task. Confine the annotation to the detail view and leave tabular renderers showing the bare status. Which commands render a status column is for the implementor to determine and confirm with the user — `task list`, `task recent` and `task show --children` are the ones observed, not necessarily the whole set.
payload.analysis:
Observed 2026-08-25 on `task show E-799 --children`. The Children table's Status column is sized by 'obsolete (replaced by E-1367)' — about 29 characters against 8-10 for a bare status — so the Title column is truncated on every row to pay for four annotated ones:

    E-810   next   unplanned                          Migrate task ordering to Lexorank strings
    E-815   next   obsolete (replaced by E-814)       Implement conflict surfacing and resolutio…
    E-893   next   obsolete (replaced by E-1367)      Consolidate Go binaries into unified endle…
    E-894   now    ready                              Move task display reads from Python to Go

The annotation is right where it was asked for. A detail view has one status and
unlimited width; a table has many rows and a shared column, so the same string
costs every row. That asymmetry is the whole defect — this is not a request to
undo E-1956.

Worth checking while in there, as evidence rather than as scope: the sibling
annotation for `duplicates` (E-1185) and `internal/sessionstatuscmd/session_status.go:885`,
which comments that it follows the same shape, so `session status` may render a
status column with the same problem.
